title: Nouns
description: Learn nouns for Grade 6: common, proper, collective, abstract, countable & uncountable nouns, plus number, gender and case — with bilingual notes, examples, practice and tests.

topics.title: Kinds of Nouns
topics.concept:
Nouns come in several types. Knowing the type helps you punctuate and use them correctly.

TypeWhat it namesExamples
Propera particular name (always capital)Diwali, Ganga, Akbar
Commona general classfestival, river, king
Collectivea group as one unitteam, flock, bunch
Abstractan idea you cannot touchcourage, beauty, anger
Concretesomething you can sensetable, rain, music

The big rule for proper nouns: they always begin with a capital letter, wherever they sit in a sentence — monday is wrong, Monday is right.

examples.problem: Name the type: The herd is grazing. (word: herd)
examples.solution: Collective noun — 'herd' names a group of animals treated as one unit.

examples.problem: Pick the abstract noun: honesty, table, dog, river
examples.solution: honesty — it names an idea you cannot see or touch; the others are concrete.

recap: Proper nouns are specific names and always take a capital letter
Collective nouns name a group as one (team, flock)
Abstract nouns name ideas/feelings you cannot touch

topics.title: Countable & Uncountable Nouns
topics.concept:
A countable noun can be counted: one book, two books. An uncountable noun cannot be counted directly: we say water, not 'two waters'.

CountableUncountable
apple, chair, ideawater, milk, advice
takes a/an, pluralsno a/an, no plural
many, a fewmuch, a little

To count an uncountable noun, add a unit: a glass of water, a piece of advice, a kilo of sugar.

examples.problem: Correct it: She gave me an advice.
examples.solution: She gave me a piece of advice. — 'advice' is uncountable, so it takes no 'an'; use a unit phrase instead.

recap: Countable nouns take a/an, plurals, and many/a few
Uncountable nouns take much/a little and never a plural -s
Count an uncountable noun with a unit: a piece of, a glass of

topics.title: Number, Gender & Case
topics.concept:
Number shows one (singular) or more (plural).

  • Regular plurals: add -s (book→books), -es (box→boxes), or change -y to -ies (city→cities).
  • Irregular plurals: child→children, man→men, tooth→teeth, mouse→mice.
  • Same form: sheep, deer, fish.

Gender: masculine (king), feminine (queen), neuter (table), common (teacher).

Case shows the noun's job: subject (Ravi runs), object (I saw Ravi), or possessive (Ravi's book; the girls' school). The apostrophe shows possession.

examples.problem: Add the apostrophe: the books belonging to the students
examples.solution: the students' books — plural ending in -s takes only an apostrophe after the s.

recap: Possessive: singular adds 's; plural ending in -s adds just '

questions.q: Which of these is a proper noun?
questions.explanation: 'Kolkata' is a specific name — a proper noun.

questions.q: The plural of 'baby' is:
questions.explanation: Consonant + y → change y to ies: babies.

questions.q: Which noun is uncountable?
questions.explanation: 'advice' is uncountable.

questions.q: Identify the collective noun: 'A swarm of bees attacked.'
questions.explanation: 'swarm' names the group as one unit.

questions.q: Which is an abstract noun?
questions.explanation: 'freedom' is an idea you cannot touch.

questions.q: The plural of 'tooth' is:
questions.explanation: Irregular plural: teeth.

questions.q: Choose the correct possessive: the bag of Sita
questions.explanation: Singular noun adds 's.

questions.q: Which word needs a capital letter?
questions.explanation: 'Monday' is a proper noun and is always capitalised.

questions.q: How ______ water is left? Choose the correct word.
questions.explanation: 'water' is uncountable, so use 'much'.

questions.q: The plural of 'sheep' is:
questions.explanation: 'sheep' is the same in singular and plural.

questions.q: Which is a concrete noun?
questions.explanation: 'mango' can be sensed; the others are abstract.

questions.q: Pick the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: 'children' is the correct plural.

questions.q: Identify the part with an error: 'A flock of geese / were / flying / over the lake.'
questions.explanation: 'A flock' is singular as one unit, so 'was flying' is correct, not 'were'.

questions.q: Choose the option that completes correctly: 'The jury ______ divided in ______ opinion.'
questions.explanation: When members act individually, the collective noun takes a plural verb: 'were ... their'.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the possessive correctly?
questions.explanation: Plural 'ladies' takes only an apostrophe: ladies'.

questions.q: Pick the correct unit phrase: '______ of lightning lit the sky.'
questions.explanation: We say 'a flash of lightning'.

questions.q: Spot the error: 'He gave me many useful informations.'
questions.explanation: 'information' is uncountable: 'much useful information'.

questions.q: Which is the abstract noun formed from 'wise'?
questions.explanation: The abstract noun of 'wise' is 'wisdom'.

questions.q: Choose the correct plural: 'two ______ of scissors'
questions.explanation: 'pairs' is the plural of the counting unit 'pair'.

questions.q: Identify the noun type of 'childhood' in 'He had a happy childhood.'
questions.explanation: 'childhood' names a period/idea — an abstract noun.

outcomes: Define a noun and identify nouns in any sentence
Tell apart common, proper, collective, abstract and concrete nouns
Decide whether a noun is countable or uncountable
Form correct plurals and use the possessive case
Answer MCQs and exam questions on nouns confidently

intro.en: A noun is a naming word. It names a person (teacher), a place (Delhi), a thing (book), or an idea (honesty). Almost every sentence you speak has at least one noun — they are the bricks of language.
intro.hi: संज्ञा (Noun) नाम बताने वाला शब्द है। यह किसी व्यक्ति (teacher), स्थान (Delhi), वस्तु (book) या भाव (honesty) का नाम बताती है। हम जो भी वाक्य बोलते हैं, उसमें लगभग हमेशा कम-से-कम एक संज्ञा होती है।

real_life.situation:
You walk into a shop and say:

You: Bhaiya, give me two notebooks, a pen, and some sugar.
real_life.why: Every important word you named — notebooks, pen, sugar — is a noun. Notice you said 'two notebooks' but 'some sugar', not 'two sugars'. That difference is the countable/uncountable idea you will master in this chapter.

rule_box.html:
A noun names a…Examples
PersonRamesh, doctor, sister
PlaceMumbai, school, garden
Thingchair, mango, phone
Idea / feelinglove, freedom, fear
rule_box.formula: Noun = name of a person, place, thing or idea
rule_box.example: In "Ravi gave kindness to the village," the nouns are Ravi, kindness, village.

words.meaning: an idea, not a physical thing

quick_test.explanation: Abstract nouns name ideas or feelings (joy, courage) that cannot be physically touched.

common_mistakes.note: Possession of a singular noun needs an apostrophe + s.
'sheep' has the same singular and plural form.

reading.passage: Meera lives in Jaipur with her family. Her courage and kindness make her popular at school. Every morning a flock of pigeons gathers on her terrace, and she gives them a handful of grain. She keeps three books, two pens and a little water on her study table.

questions.q: Write one proper noun from the passage.
questions.answer: Jaipur (or Meera) — a particular name, capitalised.

questions.q: Find one abstract noun.
questions.answer: courage (or kindness) — an idea you cannot touch.

questions.q: Which noun in the passage is uncountable?
questions.answer: water — it is counted with a unit ('a little'), never made plural.

speaking: Delhi is the capital of India.
A herd of cows is grazing in the field.
I bought two notebooks and some sugar.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences about your home, using at least one proper, one collective and one abstract noun.
writing.example: I live in Pune. My family shows great love. A bunch of keys hangs by the door.

micro_quiz.explanation: 'team' names a group treated as one unit.
'milk' cannot be counted directly; use 'a glass of milk'.

micro_quiz.q: Choose the correct possessive: 'the toys of the children'
micro_quiz.explanation: 'children' is already plural, so add 's: children's.

micro_quiz.q: Which word must always be capitalised?
micro_quiz.explanation: 'Ganga' is a proper noun and always takes a capital letter.

challenge.q: Identify the abstract noun: 'The bravery of the soldiers saved the village.'
challenge.explanation: 'bravery' names a quality you cannot touch — an abstract noun.
'information' is uncountable: no a/an, no plural; use 'some information'.
A plural noun ending in -s takes just an apostrophe: boys'.

Countable nouns take plurals and a/an; uncountable ones don't

Possessive: singular adds 's, plural-in-s adds just '
